chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qad-dah, from Abu Abdillah, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Every good deed is charity, and the one who guides to good is like the one who does it, and God loves aiding the distressed.

key_terms.الدَّالُّ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ: The one who guides to good
key_terms.كَفَاعِلِهِ: Like the doer (of the good deed)
key_terms.مَعْرُوف: Good deed or act of kindness

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for guiding someone to do good according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith establishes the comprehensive nature of charity (sadaqah) in Shia jurisprudence, extending it beyond material wealth to include all acts of goodness and guidance. It highlights the concept of 'sharing in reward' (sharikat al-thawab), where the guide is considered equal to the actor, emphasizing the communal responsibility for moral propagation. The mention of God loving those who relieve the distressed underscores the spiritual merit of alleviating suffering, a key theme in Shia ethical teachings.
